findings.title: T1059 readiness and exact OS-source receipt
evidence: A manager without Process Monitor provisioned the exact built-in object, capability, EventBus binding and fresh lifecycle/cycle boundary.
The authenticated 13-row contract named angerona.builtin.process_monitor as T1059 source.
A bounded no-op child yielded a version-3 receipt after a second Process Monitor OS reread.
A receipt-free event copying the exact live PID, birth time and token was rejected.
Release stopped and removed the temporary producer.

findings.title: Direct canonical FIM evaluator invocation mints native proof without a scan
evidence: The former public attest_fim_scan_observation surface returned an empty result.
With the exact running FIM and enrolled held marker, unrelated code called _evaluate_snapshot with a caller-created path-to-digest mapping.
No _scan call occurred and _last_scan_receipt remained complete=false/reason=not scanned.
The code-site capability minted a version-3 native_analytic_detection receipt that verify_validation_native_event accepted for T1003.
findings.impact: Same-process code can manufacture native detector efficacy while proving only that the enrolled inert marker exists with the supplied content.
findings.recommendation: Require _evaluate_snapshot to consume a one-use authenticated result produced only by a complete internal _scan generation and bind root coverage, exact snapshot digest, per-object identity/change token, and lifecycle. Strong closure requires a measured isolated producer with a private key/channel; otherwise label the result same-process simulation validation rather than native analytic detection.

findings.title: Issuer-owned verifier dispatch is still ordinary mutable Python state
evidence: The former module-global callable alias no longer controls dispatch.
The replacement callable fields remain on _LeaseAuthorityState, reachable through _lease_authority(lease) and the module-global weak registry.
Replacing only state.verify_native_impl made the public wrapper accept a receipt-free row without altering the lease class or former alias.
findings.impact: An admitted Python extension can redirect evidence verification and invalidate an immutable/issuer-only in-process assurance claim.
findings.recommendation: Move verifier code, keys, replay state and result signing into a measured restricted process or service and expose only an opaque handle/public verification key. Until then, describe the capture as accidental-tamper resistance, not an immutable verifier boundary.

findings.title: Cleanup exact-object custody
evidence: A replacement before DELETE-handle acquisition caused fail-closed retention.
A replacement after the exact DELETE-capable handle opened survived unchanged while only the enrolled renamed original was disposed.
The POSIX branch moves to unpredictable same-directory custody and verifies the moved inode before unlink.

findings.title: Rolling back only the AAR journal recreates an authenticated sequence fork
evidence: Normal fixed-file rollback advanced to sequence 3 and cooperative publication remains OS-serialized.
Restoring only the ordinary writable journal to its authentic report-1 prefix while leaving report-2 fixed files intact caused the publisher to repair the fixed files backward.
The next report became a different HMAC-valid sequence-2 descendant of report 1; the resulting journal chain validated.
verified_aar_handoff_text accepted the new fork because it verifies report/head bytes but not journal inclusion or an independent high-water.
findings.impact: A same-user writer can hide an intervening report and bind review/remediation to a validly signed rolled-back branch.
findings.recommendation: Anchor every accepted AAR journal transition to a separately administered monotonic CAS authority using an authenticated precommit outbox, retain and revalidate the journal object across load/append, and make GUI handoff verify the exact signed journal row plus witnessed head. Without that witness, call the local journal tamper-evident rather than rollback-resistant.

findings.title: Maximum admitted TTL evidence horizon
evidence: The authenticated 4,235-second campaign horizon overrode the 3,600-second caller default while remaining below the 4,500-second cap.
A separately signed history ending 1 ms beyond its admitted TTL failed lease history verification.

findings.title: Zero-step planned denominator
evidence: An independent signed zero-step incomplete Red Team history persisted an authenticated report.
The report contained 14 diagnostic verdicts, denominator/detection_steps 13, coverage_score_eligible=false and a null simulation-validation rate.

assurance_boundary: The closed cases validate inert local simulation contracts only. The reopened cases require same-process Python execution or same-user local report-state write access and affect evidence truth/continuity, not host compromise.
